ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An amusement park ride consists of a large spinning cylinder of radius \( r \) with rough walls. At a given angular velocity \( \omega \), the horizontal floor of the cylinder drops, but a rider of mass \( m \) remains safely pinned against the walls of the cylinder. What is the minimum coefficient of static friction \( \mu \) necessary for the rider to keep from sliding down the wall?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a large cylinder rotating around a vertical central axis; the dashed line represents the vertical axis of rotation, and the arrow at the top and the symbol omega indicate that the cylinder rotates with angular velocity omega. The person is pressed against the vertical side wall of the cylinder, indicating that the supporting force of the wall on the person is horizontal, pointing toward the center of the cylinder; the person may slide downward along the vertical direction and needs static friction to prevent it. Then reason: Analyze the forces on the rider in an inertial frame. In the horizontal direction, the normal force N of the wall on the person provides the centripetal force required for circular motion, so N = m r omega^2. In the vertical direction, the floor has already dropped; if the person is just not sliding down, the maximum static friction force is upward and balances gravity, namely f_s,max = mu N = mg. Substituting N gives mu m r omega^2 = mg, therefore the minimum static friction coefficient is mu_min = g/(r omega^2).

method.method_draft: Use an inertial-frame free-body diagram of the rider. Read from the image that the rider is pressed against the vertical cylindrical wall while the cylinder rotates about its central vertical axis; the wall normal is horizontal and points toward the center. Read from the text that the cylinder has radius r, angular speed omega, rough walls, and the rider must not slide down after the floor drops. In the horizontal direction, the wall's normal force supplies the required centripetal force: N = m r omega^2. In the vertical direction, static friction acts upward to balance weight at the threshold: f_s,max = mu N = mg. Solve mu m r omega^2 = mg, giving mu_min = g/(r omega^2).

method.method_draft: Use the rider's rotating frame, where the rider is momentarily at rest relative to the cylinder wall. Read from the image that the rider is stationary relative to the rotating wall and that the wall contact is radial. Read from the text that the floor is gone, so only the wall's normal force and friction can support the rider. In the rotating frame, introduce the outward centrifugal pseudo-force m omega^2 r. The wall's normal reaction balances this horizontally, so N = m omega^2 r. Vertically, the only upward support is static friction, whose maximum is mu N. Require mu N >= mg; for the minimum, set mu m omega^2 r = mg and obtain mu_min = g/(r omega^2).
